analysis: All changes are test-only files under provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests: SandboxStatusTests.swift (new workDisks test, head lines 78-100, status rendering of the add-on's `disks` array), SandboxTestSupport.swift (fake installer script gains `planStandardError` and `workDisks` parameters, head lines 187-201), and the new SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift (`darkbloom sandbox setup --disk`). No production code is modified, so there is no runtime change to TB-013/T-061 (installer download and add-on command run as the Mac's owner), TB-012/T-059/T-060 (add-on hold socket), or T-041 (cache storage). The fake installer scripts are written to temporary directories and only run in tests. The shell quoting helper `quoted` escapes single quotes, and fixtures are static strings, so no injection path exists in the test harness. The tests reference production symbols (SandboxWorkDisk.Volume, SandboxInstaller.diskOption, SandboxAddonStatus.disks/supportsWorkDisks) that this batch does not show. The new `--disk` feature lets the CLI pass operator-supplied paths to the add-on installer, and the tests mention ownership-enabled and APFS checks. The production implementation (path validation, ownership and root-volume handling, the plan parsing and confirmation flow) belongs to a separate batch. The next pass should check that the `--disk` arguments forwarded to the root-owner-run installer are validated, and that the TB-013 threat entry covers this new surface. The SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift patch is truncated and has no numbered source unit, so I could not read its remaining content. I record this as a coverage limit rather than a finding.
